newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks tumbled on Monday on a bleak outlook on exchange control abolition and a presistently high money market shortage, fuelling fears of a rate hike, dealers said.
Industrial stocks were hardest hit with the index diving over one percent as futures arbitrage players sold off stock in the spot market.
"There is no light at the end of the tunnel," one dealer said.
"The money market shortage is up, interest rates look to be going up, inflation is higher and now exchange controls are going to be around for a long time," the dealer said.
The high shortage, stubbornly holding above the nine billion rand level, was seen making a hike in the central Bank rate and commercial banks' prime rate inevitable, sooner or later.
The latest on exchange controls came from Central Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals who on Friday told Reuters abolition would be a gradual process which could take four to five years.
Dealers said this was in the long term detrimental to the rand as it would invite speculation which in turn was damaging to the equity market, keeping foreigners out.
"Foreigners especially want to know some sort of top (for the rand) before they will readily invest in our market," another dealer said.

Traders said futures players had sold off stock in the spot market taking advantage of contracts' discount to fair value. At the same time, futures were sold off as the same negative factors as beset the spot market, weighed on futures.
"Players have been offloading long positions, cutting their losses as the market shows little sign of bouncing," a futures trader said.
They said volumes had been thin, exaggerating the fall.
"The recent volatility on the rand has been a major headache for foreigners. They have been very much absent from the market."

A recent batch of poor corporate results, notably from subidiaries of heavyweight stock SAB, depressed the stock market further, with the outlook for SAB's half year results due on Wednesday not so rosy, dealers said.
The industrial index shed 99.9 points to 7,891.9 lopping 60.8 points off the all share index which finished at 6,732.7.
December industrial futures dived almost 200 points to last trade at 7,490/99 from 7,670 before, with the all-share contract at finishing at 6,090/100 from 6,190 previously.
Anglo lost 550 cents to 272 rand, SAB was off 200 cents to 116.50 rand, Liberty downed 225 cents to 125 rand and FNB cast off 90 cents to 23 rand.
Traders said the outlook for industrial stocks and futures on Tuesday remained grim as the negative factors hanging over the market would not go away in a hurry.

On the gold board, a slightly firmer bullion price could not offset the market's overall pessimism leaving the index 2.3 points weaker at 1,678.8. The near-month gold contract was little moved at 1,212/20 from 1,213 on Friday.
Vaal Reefs lost 300 cents to 340 rand, but Dries lifted 75 cents to 59.25 rand.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
